entities.evidence: Abram, the traveler who goes down to Egypt, is Terah’s son, later named Abraham.
The directional ending on מִצְרַיְמָה marks Egypt as Abram’s destination, and “to sojourn there” confirms the place.

review.translation: [Then there was|0] [a famine|1] [in the land|2], [so|3] [Abram|4] [went down|3] [to Egypt|5] [to sojourn|6] [there|7] [because|8] [the famine|10] [{was}|9] [severe|9] [in the land|11].

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רָעָב בָּאָרֶץ introduces a famine in the land. The later phrase כָבֵד הָרָעָב refers back to that famine and gives its severity as the reason Abram went down to Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, agreeing with רָעָב ‘famine’.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי רָעָב בָּאָרֶץ introduces a famine in the land. The later phrase כִּי כָבֵד הָרָעָב בָּאָרֶץ refers back to that famine and gives its severity as the reason Abram went to Egypt.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: A shortage of food affecting a region.

analysis.evidence: The famine is in the land where Abram has been staying. Its severity prompts him to go down to Egypt, so the noun refers to the territory he leaves.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ incorporates the definite article and precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute state. אָרֶץ is the pausal form of אֶרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: אַבְרָם is the subject, and the directional ending on מִצְרַיְמָה marks Egypt as his destination. Abram went down to Egypt to stay there because the famine was severe.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.
analysis.sense: go down to a land or city

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרֶד אַבְרָם מִצְרַיְמָה, “Abram went down to Egypt,” אַבְרָם names the subject of וַיֵּרֶד and refers to the same man named in Genesis 12:4.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּרֶד אַבְרָם means “Abram went down.” מִצְרַיְמָה names his destination, and לָגוּר שָׁם (“to sojourn there”) confirms that Egypt is the place where he intended to stay.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper place name with directional ־ָה marking the destination of motion.

analysis.evidence: Abram went down to Egypt לָגוּר שָׁם, “to sojourn there,” because the famine was severe in the land. שָׁם refers to Egypt, where Abram intended to stay as a foreign resident.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לָ־ introduces a Qal infinitive construct expressing the purpose of Abram’s journey.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68616:14, 68615:11, 68383:28, 68361:6, 68359:3, 68354:8, 66060:4, 66059:10, 66056:7.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adverb of place with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there. The clause כָבֵד הָרָעָב בָּאָרֶץ says that the famine was severe in the land.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כִּי כָבֵד הָרָעָב בָּאָרֶץ means “because the famine was severe in the land.” The famine’s severity explains why Abram went down to Egypt.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective serving as the predicate of הָרָעָב, “the famine.”

analysis.evidence: The verse first introduces רָעָב, “a famine,” then refers back to it with the definite article in כִּי כָבֵד הָרָעָב בָּאָרֶץ, “because the famine was severe in the land.” Its severity explains why Abram went to Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: A shortage of food affecting a region.

analysis.evidence: The final בָּאָרֶץ repeats the location given at the start of the verse. The famine was severe in the land where Abram had been living, which explains why he went down to Egypt.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ incorporates the definite article and precedes a common noun of both genders in the singular absolute. אָרֶץ is the pausal form of אֶרֶץ.
